answer: Attestation weight can be tied to a slow-built track record instead of account count. A new identity starts as a relic-free blank: no graded history, so its votes count for little. Reputation forms like a pearl, one thin layer per epoch of work that peers actually scored. A sybil farm can spin up a thousand clones, but each one must grow its own history separately, and that crystal-clear cost per fake identity outweighs anything the swarm could extract.
